nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Loss of coastal wetlands_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How much has the extent of inland wetlands declined?
nodes.answer: The extent of inland wetlands has declined by an estimated 75%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Loss of coastal wetlands_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the two primary drivers of biodiversity loss mentioned in the text?
nodes.answer: The two primary drivers are the ongoing reclamation and degradation of inland wetlands and agricultural intensification.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Loss of coastal wetlands_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What action was taken in the central-eastern Po Plain to support biodiversity conservation?
nodes.answer: The application of biodiversity conservation actions helped create low-water wetlands with plenty of mudflats.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Loss of coastal wetlands_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which bird species is now nesting in the created low-water wetlands in the Po Plain?
nodes.answer: Northern lapwings are nesting in the created low-water wetlands.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Loss of coastal wetlands_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What major finding relates to East Coast and West Coast estuaries in terms of climate change vulnerability?
nodes.answer: East Coast estuaries are highly vulnerable to climate change, while West Coast estuaries may serve as future thermal refugia for MHWs.
